BLOCKER: Design does not answer the DESIGN GUARDRAILS checklist (reversibility, authz/RLS, blast radius, invariants, rollback, observability); Gate 1.5 approval is invalid while these are unaddressed (CL-006/CL-008).

Gate 1 context fields `out_of_scope`, `affected_components`, `affected_files`, `risks` are all "Not specified" — no scope boundary or risk register, so delta review and encoding-gate blast radius cannot be bounded.
MAJOR: Encoding gate scope ("changed source/config/docs", working-tree/untracked files) is undefined relative to the review base/head binding — unclear which commit/tree is authoritative, risking false pass/fail and non-reproducible evidence.
No statement of how prior findings/dispositions are stored, keyed, and invalidated across rebases; without a stable base/head binding, delta reviews can silently drop or resurrect findings.
Design-pack enforced items (failure matrix, test matrix, rollout/rollback, decisions) have no defined schema/owner or failure mode when an item is missing — validation behaviour unspecified.
Language rule not explicitly addressed: which components of design-pack generation, encoding gate, and re-review delta logic are new shipped logic (must be Go) vs tooling (Python allowed).
No observability plan for the new gates (metrics/log lines on gate failure, which surface, who is alerted) — failures may be silent.
Rollback is only "Revert the change" with no migration-interrupted/recovery path for any persisted design-pack or last_reviewed_HEAD state (guardrail 6).
MINOR: Recurring gaps unaddressed in this design: `_render_review`/`_item_dispositions` lack path-level tests (index alignment, missing item, unknown status).
Redaction coverage limited to query params; encoding/gate evidence may include headers or path fragments.
Double `resp.Body.Close()` noted but not scheduled for cleanup in scope.
NIT: Probe-key uniqueness via wall-clock nanos — negligible but worth an injectable clock for test determinism.
`in_scope` duplicates `approach` verbatim; consider distinct statements for auditability.
SUMMARY: Verdict: design is not ready for Gate 1 — guardrail checklist unanswered and required Gate 1 metadata missing.
Top risks: undefined delta-review base/head binding, unspecified language-rule split, silent gate failures with no observability, and rollback limited to a revert.
Address BLOCKER/MAJOR items and pre-empt recurring test/redaction findings before proceeding.
